system.summary: simple substitution, one number per letter (1-54), numbers separated by points, inside clear text; a = 35, b = 31 ... p = 1 going down by two, q = 36, r = 38 ... u = 44 going up; 20 is a second c

prior_solution.where: period marginal decipherments (fols. 127r, 200, 106); period clear copy fol. 182; É. Longin (ed.), "Le siège de Dole par le prince de Condé (27 mai - 15 août 1636). Documents inédits", Mémoires et documents inédits pour servir à l'histoire de la Franche-Comté, vol. X, Besançon, 1912 (archive.org mmoiresetdocum10acaduoft): nos. LIV (pp. 89-90), CXXXII (pp. 190-191), CLXXVIII (pp. 249-251), CCLXXXVII (p. 405), from Brun's drafts (Buthiers archives, Brun papers vol. VII), the words to be enciphered printed in brackets. Key not printed (Longin gives none; Antoine Rossignol broke the cipher in July 1636). Nothing in this repository or on DECODE (4 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the volume and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out check, prior-work search before publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up.

solution.what: Key learnt on fol. 200 block 1 aligned 1:1 with its period marginal gloss (177 numbers), majority letter per number, frozen.
One measurement on held-out fol. 200 block 2 (341 numbers) against its gloss: 0.9072 vs 200 shuffled keys max 0.229.
Unglossed passages of fols. 191, 127v, 181 and 183 read with the key unchanged.
Clear text found printed in Longin 1912 (from Brun's drafts) after the reading; fol. 182 is a period clear copy of fols. 181/183.
Letter agreement with Longin 1912: 0.967 on fols. 191 + 127v; fol. 183 vs fol. 182 identical apart from vous/nous, ou/a.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key learnt from the period marginal decipherment of fol. 200 block 1, validated on block 2.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule, mechanical count (reading.md): fols. 191 + 127v 128 words, 113 certain, 11 probable, 0 restored, 4 unresolved.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): protocol hashed before measurement; key frozen; one measurement on fol. 200 block 2 (341 numbers) against its period gloss: letters 0.9072 vs 200 shuffled-key controls max 0.229 (mean 0.1309); thresholds 0.85 and max+0.30 fixed in advance.

texts.label: The Parlement of Dole, 22 July 1636 (fol. 200r, both blocks glossed in the margin)
texts.summary: On 22 July the Parlement of Dole praises the relief army's resolution to come without delay, admits some slight danger in an arrival put off too long, and says it is better to risk something than to lose everything, hoping all will go to their glory and the confusion of their enemies. The text is the period marginal gloss, which the key was learnt from and tested on.

reading_review.note: Both blocks read as continuous French sentences from the period marginal decipherment; block 1 (177 numbers) gave the key and block 2 (341 numbers) tested it at 0.9072 of letters. Not a blind reading: the gloss is the plaintext.

texts.label: A. Brun, [1 July 1636] (fol. 191) and the Parlement, 7 June 1636 (fol. 127v)
texts.summary: On 1 July (fol. 191) Brun writes that they must come as soon as possible with the cavalry relief sent by “His Most Serene Highness” (not identified here), without going to join it at Salins; that letting four or five days pass is a great risk; he recalls the diversions, the signals and recognition marks, the cutting of the enemy’s communications; an attack by day would be more honourable and more useful than by night. They are to bring rations, flour and corn, with tools to reap; the Gray garrison is to burn Rigny, Talmay, Pontailler and Mirebeau, and above all destroy the forge of Drambon and the others where the bombs thrown on Dole are made; raids are to go into the Duchy, Bassigny and Bresse.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 4 Nov 2026 (French): fol. 191 reads throughout as Brun's instructions (come at once with the cavalry relief, do not go to Salins, signals and diversions, attack by day, bring rations and harvest tools, burn Rigny, Talmay, Pontailler, Mirebeau and the Drambon forge where the bombs are made); fol. 127v "c'est[oit] un piège pour l'ennemi". 128 words, 113 certain, 11 probable, 0 restored, 4 unresolved = 96.9%. Checked afterwards against Longin 1912 (letter agreement 0.967).

texts.label: Commis au gouvernement, 25 June 1636 (fols. 181 and 183; clear copy fol. 182)
texts.summary: On 25 June (fols. 181, 183; clear on fol. 182) the commis describe the French quarters: on the side of the bridge, a separate attack with three or four hundred horse and six hundred foot; elsewhere, an attack of twelve hundred men.

reading_review.note: fol. 183 read with the key and compared with the period clear copy fol. 182: identical apart from vous/nous and ou/a; 27 words, 21 certain, 6 probable.
